description: 3-bedroom apartment with 1 master suite (en-suite bathroom) and 2 single bedrooms. The 2 single bedrooms can each function independently as a bedroom, home office, hobby room or guest room in any combination. Total area 135 sqm. Kitchen island present — hob is located on the island, sink on the long wall countertop. The person cooking at the island directly faces the dining table and seating area. The wall countertop runs along the 9m width of the room, allowing a continuous cabinet run of up to 9m with potential for full-height storage cabinets and large appliances. No wall separates the kitchen from the dining and seating area — suited to someone who wants to cook while remaining part of a group or supervising children in the same space. Living area furniture arrangement is linear: kitchen — dining — living in one continuous line along the 9m width of the room. A storage room is present adjacent to the kitchen, usable as pantry, general storage or laundry room. The living-kitchen room faces the 9m bottom facade. All three bedrooms face the 15m right facade, each with a full exterior wall. The apartment is double-aspect overall. Master bedroom 27 sqm with en-suite bathroom 9.8 sqm and walk-in wardrobe — open wardrobe area with two facing storage units separated from the sleeping area by a single wall, no closing door. The master suite is positioned at the far end of the apartment from the entry and living area, with the two secondary bedrooms between it and the living zone — this gives the master the greatest acoustic separation and privacy. Access from the master bedroom to the kitchen is via a straight corridor with no intermediate door, a reasonable distance but longer than in a compact layout. Secondary bedroom 1: 15.2 sqm with desk shown in plan. Secondary bedroom 2: 14.7 sqm with desk shown in plan. Both secondary bedrooms are accessed from the central corridor with a closing door, providing acoustic separation from the living area. Each secondary bedroom is large enough to accommodate a bunk bed for two siblings. Possible configurations for the two secondary bedrooms — these are mutually exclusive: (1) two children's bedrooms; (2) one children's bedroom and one home office or hobby room; (3) two home offices or hobby rooms; (4) one or both as guest rooms; (5) one or both as siblings' bunk bed rooms, extending total household capacity to 5 or 6 people. This layout cannot simultaneously provide two separate children's bedrooms and a dedicated home office without using a bunk bed arrangement in one of them. Two bathrooms allow parallel morning routines for a household of three to four, or five to six in a bunk bed configuration. Corridor 14.6 sqm connects all bedrooms to entry and living. Entry area 3.7 sqm provides sufficient space for coat and shoe storage at the entrance. Entry opens directly into the corridor which connects without a door to the living-kitchen area — no door separates the entrance from the kitchen. Suits households that prioritise communal cooking and dining, families with one or two children, couples using secondary rooms flexibly, and people working from home in a dedicated closed room.
not_suitable_for: household with no use for secondary rooms
jurisdictions requiring door separation between entry hall and kitchen
household requiring two separate children's bedrooms AND a dedicated home office simultaneously without bunk bed arrangement
